notes: Main-split ABox revision of a stored fact (15 queries), migrated 2026-11-12 from the earlier TCP record. The edit stays (TCP is connection-oriented: 862 exact hits, in Wikipedia's first paragraph). connection_mode is functional (a protocol has one mode), which gives the related near question. The related far question is the TCP versus UDP contrast, stated in every networking text. Every route to a determinate derived answer goes through TCP's mode alone; every question about what TCP does (the handshake, closing a connection, HTTP over TCP) is stored by name and is therefore left to the one indeterminate query. The earlier HTTP-over-TCP questions were dropped for that reason (a stored description of HTTP's transport competes with the edit), and the fill-in-the-blank wording the audit flagged was rephrased as plain questions. The binding question reaches TCP through RFC 793, a document number a model holds separately. Counts are exact-phrase counts in Dolma (v4_dolma-v1_7_llama) except those marked approximate. Task balance of the topic: application and inheritance are carried by the Silicon Valley record (technology-replace-0004). Revised 2026-11-12 after review: the indeterminate query was the three-way handshake, but a connectionless TCP that still opens with a handshake contradicts the definition, so w1 was not a valid world. It now asks whether TCP guarantees complete, in-order delivery, which a model can keep by name or lose with the connection mode; the bridge check (a connectionless protocol keeps no record of what it has sent) is audit-pending.
